title: When Numbers Tell Half the Story: Human-Metric Alignment in Topic Model Evaluation
venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference (LREC 2026)
subcategory: human evaluation: word intrusion and new Topic Word Mixing task
task: Checking whether coherence/diversity metrics match human judgement in a specialised domain
problem: Coherence and diversity metrics were validated mostly on general-domain corpora, and no human task existed for inter-topic distinctness.
architecture: Topic Word Mixing (TWM): annotators see 8 words from one topic or from the two most similar topics (topic embeddings = mean of top-50 word vectors from stella_en_1.5B_v5) and decide whether one or two topics are present. Word intrusion (TWI): 4 top words + 1 frequency-matched intruder. 18 models (6 methods x about 10, 25, 50 topics), 10 trained annotators, nearly 4,000 annotations; intrusion accuracy adjusted for intruder-topic similarity.

datasets.name: Philosophy of science publications
datasets.details: 16,917 full-text articles from eight journals (1931-2017), about 65 million tokens

key_results: Top2Vec has the best CV (0.72-0.80) and diversity (0.98-1) but the lowest word-intrusion accuracy (0.693); BERTopic has low CV (0.52-0.62) but the highest intrusion accuracy (0.900).
Word intrusion agreement: 80.3%, Fleiss' kappa 0.688; TWM agreement 77.1%, kappa 0.270.
Intrusion accuracy correlates negatively with intruder-topic similarity (r = -0.145, p = 0.0079).
strengths: Introduces a human counterpart to topic-diversity metrics and releases about 4,000 annotations.
Shows that intruder selection needs semantic-similarity control in specialised domains.

limitations.text: Coherence and diversity capture only part of topic quality; coverage is not evaluated by humans.
Single domain-specific corpus; TWM agreement is only fair (kappa 0.270).
